questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I knew that I wanted to go outside of Europe, and I wanted a university that was in either a really big city or in beautiful nature. Toronto definitely offered the big city.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There wasn't really a whole lot of information to find. University of Toronto uses the same system as Absalon, and the small bit of information needed was on there. When I had questions, the Centre for International Experience at UofT was very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, the Faculty of Arts and Science did not do any real introduction week (but I believe that other faculties do). This meant that there was no form of introduction before classes started. The Centre for International Experience offered some exchange-events and campus tours later in the school year, but it would have been nice if there was something before classes started.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I just found an apartment on Airbnb. Really expensive but very easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus isn't an issue at all, as long as you don't live too far away. Public transport in Toronto is somewhat questionable if you don't live close to the main subway lines (1 or 2), so make sure that you are either within bike/walk distance or live by these subway lines. The busses and trams are horrible.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't really know how it works to be fair

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UofT made it really easy to apply for courses, and except for one course, I got everything I applied for. Main issue is that they upload the course catalog quite late and do a lot of changes each semester, so what you had pre-approved might not be what's offered now.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Once the course catalog was ready they opened up for course registration. For the fall-2025 semester they opened for course registration June 6th. There were three rounds where you could apply for five courses each round (KU students need 4 courses to reach 30ects).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The course platform was very helpful once it was updated with what courses were actually available and they also had a few guides online. Centre for International Experience was helpful as well

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted except for one in round 1, and then I got the last one I needed in round 2. No issues really.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for everything that sounds remotely relevant in round 1 cause most fill up quickly. You can always drop courses if you have too many or you find something more exciting.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UofT were a great help with everything. The only difficult thing was getting KU to pre-approve courses...

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
BA courses were a bit easier than at KU. Took a 200 course (2nd year) which was extremely easy, while 300 & 400 courses were probably about the same level as back home with way higher expectations than the 200 course.
The one MA course I took was extremely high level, but it was also a boutique course with only 20 students from a special IR program.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You are expected to participate in class, and you are graded based on your oral participation. Also way more assignments and midterm exams. Actually it feels a bit like gymnasiet, but it makes you participate more. About the same amount of reading at home as at KU, but fewer hours of classes throughout the week (I had 9 hours in class every week)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
POL218H1 F (Fall) State, Society and Power in Comparative Perspective.
POL311H1 F (Fall) Law and Political Development.
POL358H1 F (Fall) Conflicts, Minority Rights and Para-States in Europe.
POL466H1 F (Fall) Topics in International Politics III - Dealing with dictators.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
POL218H1 F (Fall) State, Society and Power in Comparative Perspective was an extremely boring and overly easy courses with a bad professor. Only took it cause it was the only course KU would pre-approve, but it was a waste of time.

The other courses were amazing, and I can't recommend the professors enough. If in any way possible, take a course with Professor-NAME REDACTED-, a UofT legend who is so different from any other teaching professionals I have ever met.

Professor -NAME REDACTED- (Topics in International Politics III - Dealing with dictators) is also a rock star in the IR field, so try to take her courses if possible if you like IR.

Law and Political Development was a little too law-based for me, but professor -NAME REDACTED- was extremely nice and talented. Also the tests and exams were really easy so it wasn't that stressful.

Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *

Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: On top of your own health insurance you have to purchase the UHIP one from the university. However it's money well spent. They paid for everything when I broke my wrist.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Going out to eat is cheaper than in Copenhagen and beers and also way cheaper. However, groceries are extremely expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UofT St. George has three huge sports facilities that students can use for free (gyms, tracks, indoor and outdoor basketball/pickleball/badminton/tennis courts). You can also access most museums for free on certain days as a UofT student.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
You can participate in multiple sports leagues at UofT (Varsity, tri-campus & intramural). However, I did not get any information about this from UofT and had to do all of the research myself. Make sure to do this as you have to sign up essentially right when you get there. I did not participate throughout the semester as I broke my wrist during tri-campus tryouts, but it seems like a great way to make friends.

There is also a club for literally everything. I did not sign up for any, but did participate at a food-event with the Georgian society club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Would recommend trying everything! Why not?

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Toronto is massive, so you can visit new places every week. 
Would definitely recommend going to Banff.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer:
Extremely easy do to the many cultures in Toronto. It really is the melting pot of the world! 
However, there are so many exchange students at UofT that you're not special, so don't expect any free points for being an exchange student (About 30% of the students at UofT are international students). You have to actively do something to make friends and meet people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The other KU students and I always joke about not having made a single Canadian friend. The other exchange students are generally more outgoing. Try to join the events set up by the Centre for International Experience and join a sports team.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: No matter which cuisine you want on any given day, you can definitely find it in Toronto. Also a great shopping culture if you want to spend all of your money late at night with all clothing stores staying open till 9pm.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Get a Bike Share Toronto membership! Toronto is a fairly good biking city, and you can get unlimited bike rentals for a year for 300kr. as a UofT student.
Try to be social in the beginning - It's probably the most overwhelming time, but it's when everybody are looking for friends.
It might look cool, but don't live down by the water. It's really boring when it gets cold.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: UofT publishes their exam dates extremely late (2-3 weeks before the actual exams). Don't wait for this to buy your plane ticket home unless you want to spend 10000kr on a one-way home for Christmas. Just look up the last possible exam date and work from there.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: First of all I thought that the professors were amazing and that the academic experience was extremely rewarding. Also, Toronto is an amazing city to live in, and you will never get bored. It is crazy but so much fun! I can't recommend it enough.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer:
The greatest challenge before and during was trying to get KU to pre-approve courses and everything else. It felt like they worked against us and not with us. Felt like giving up on the whole thing multiple times because the process was so frustrating. The people at KU-abroad were very nice, but the whole process was insane. It killed the excitement and even 2 months before the start of the semester I wasn't sure if I would be able to go.
Once here, there were no great challenges (other than missing my mom of course).

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Something has to be done about the process leading up to exchange. 

Do your exchange at The University of Toronto (St. George). I can't think of a better city/university combination. 10/10

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
